story_text:
Bringing back the 90s and 2000s clear tech craze.
Back then, see-through gadgets were everywhere. Today the original clear consoles, like the Game Boy, sell at collector prices, and new tech is boring and grey.
[画像: Arduview clipped to a set of keys by a window; its screen reads World’s First Transparent Game Console]
Meet Arduview, the keychain game console where everything is clear.
- Fully transparent: shell, circuit board and screen.
- Pocket sized: you won’t notice it on you.
- Always with you: it hangs from your keyring.
- Instantly play community favorites: 300+ built-in retro games.
- Open to tinkering: put new games on it or write one yourself, with a big community behind you.
[画像: Six photos of the Arduview prototype: a game playing in hand, the ArduView logo on screen, a close-up of the clear board and buttons, a game-over screen on a desk, a macro of the screen’s pixels, and a hand holding it lit up]
[画像: Section heading: As seen in]
[画像: Press quotes. Yahoo Tech: “A crystal shell handheld with a see-through motherboard, using a transparent display.” Tom’s Hardware: “The makers of this device have fully embraced the latest in transparent electronics.” Android Headlines: “The Arduview handheld looks no bigger than a credit card.” Hackster.io: “That is a transparent OLED, so it is like viewing glowing blue pixels on a clear piece of glass.”]
[画像: Also covered by Notebookcheck, Ground News, The Awesomer, ShiftDelete.Net, GSMDome, Merlin’in Kazani, LavX News and Retro Dodo]
[画像: Section heading: Not just the shell]
[画像: Heading: Through the screen]
[画像: A face seen through Arduview’s shell, board and lit screen while a game plays]
Lit pixels glow cyan and the rest of the screen stays clear, so you see the board behind the game. Switched off, it looks like smoked glass. The OLED makes its own light, so you can read it in daylight and in the dark.
[画像: Heading: How the layers fit]
[画像: Render: the shell, screen and circuit board come together into one Arduview]
Render. Screen simulated.
[画像: Section heading: Take it anywhere]
[画像: Heading: Clips onto your keys]
[画像: Arduview hanging from a keyring by a window, swaying, Circuit Dude on screen]
Every unit has a keyring hole and a clip; a ring is available as a $9 add-on.
[画像: Heading: Ultra portable]
[画像: Two hands playing Arduview, then it slides into a trouser pocket]
Take it out, play with it, put it back. It’s about as long as a credit card.
[画像: To scale: a clear Game Boy, a smartphone, a credit card and Arduview side by side. Arduview is about as long as the credit card and narrower.]
[画像: 300+ built-in games. Title screens in glowing cyan pixels: Arduventure, Ardynia, Catacombs of the Damned, Circuit Dude, Evade 2, Micro City, Hopper, Mini Rogue, Space Cab, Rooftop Rescue, Quadrastic and Lasers]
[画像: Top picks by genre. RPG and adventure: Arduventure, Ardynia, Dark & Under, Glove, Star Honor. Shooters: Catacombs of the Damned, Virus LQP-79, Evade 2. Platformers: Mystic Balloon, Omega Horizon, Castle Boy. Puzzle: Circuit Dude, Quadrastic, Ardulem, PiCross. Arcade and action: Hopper, Rooftop Rescue, Space Cab, Kemono Patrol. Simulation and strategy: Micro City, Tacklebox, MicroTD. Racing and sports: Crazy Kart, ArduBall, Reverse Mermaid Hockey. Board and card: Solitaire, Reversi, Farkle.]
A few favorites from the Arduboy library.
It doesn’t run emulators or Game Boy games, on purpose. Every game was written for its chip, the ATmega32U4.
[画像: Open platform, load your favorite games: a code editor shows an Arduboy game sketch next to Arduview, with three steps: pick a game, load it, play it]
Arduview is independent of Arduboy but compatible with it. The code library, the tools and most of the games are free at arduboy.com. To add a game, plug Arduview into your computer over USB-C and open the Arduboy Web Flasher in Chrome.
To write your own, install the free Arduino editor and work through Crait’s seven-part tutorial on the Arduboy forum. It starts with setup and ends with a working Pong. You can also try many of them free in your browser at arduboy.ried.cl.
[画像: Section heading: Hardware]
[画像: Close-up of Arduview’s controls through the clear shell: the D-pad on the left, the A and B buttons on the right]
[画像: Specs. Display: 1.51-inch transparent OLED, 128 × 64. Size: 85 × 43 × 13 mm. Weight: 50 g, about an egg. Chip: ATmega32U4, the same 8-bit chip as the Arduboy. Storage: 16 MB flash. Port: USB-C, for charging and loading games. Battery: 130 mAh, charges in about 50 minutes. Online: none, no Wi-Fi, app store or account. Sound: built-in speaker.]
[画像: Said before launch: scrolling comments from early supporters on Facebook and Messenger, such as “Transparent screen looks cool” and “Really looking forward to this thing”. Comments, not reviews; some are shortened.]
Questions are welcome in the comments here.
[画像: Section heading: What your pledge pays for]
[画像: Clip from our production update: a hand turning a clear Arduview shell over a bench of parts]
From our production update on October 21, 2026.
[画像: Two production photos: clear Arduview cases and back covers laid out on a table, and a box of circuit boards packed in foam]
We’ve picked a manufacturer, received production quotes and arranged packaging and shipping. What’s left needs money up front: molds for the resin shell and the buttons, and setting up the assembly line. Your pledge covers that tooling and the first units off the line.
[画像: Rewards, up to 52% off retail. One Arduview: Launch Special $73 (51% off), Super Early Bird $89 (40% off), Early Bird $99 (34% off), Collector $149 retail price. Two Pack $149 ($74.50 each). Four Pack $289 ($72.25 each). Add-ons: keyring $9, display stand $19. Shipping $19 to $39 by region, charged after the campaign.]
You’re only charged if we reach the goal, when the campaign ends. You can change or cancel your pledge any time before then.
[画像: Stretch goals. At $100K, a multicolor option so backers can choose their shell color, shown as concept renders in cyan, red and pink. At $200K, a hard carry pouch with every pledge.]
[画像: FAQs. Will it run original Arduboy games? Yes, it runs the existing Arduboy library as-is, no re-flashing. Battery life: being measured on production units. Sound: yes, through the built-in speaker. Taxes and import duties: confirmed per country before the pledge manager opens. More answers are in the FAQ tab.]
[画像: Section heading: When it ships]
[画像: Timeline: first prototype, Sep 2025. Early units sent to reviewers, Sep 2026. Kickstarter launch, Oct 27, 2026 (you are here). First production run, Dec 2026 to Jan 2027. Shipping begins, Feb 2027.]
These dates are our plan, not a guarantee. If anything moves, we’ll post an update.
[画像: Shipping and delivery. We ship worldwide, directly from China. Shipping is charged after the campaign ends, by region: Asia $19, Europe $25, North America $25, South America $35, Africa $35, everywhere else $39. Delivery takes about a month on average. If it arrives broken, we replace it free within 30 days. Every Arduview comes with a USB-C cable and a manual.]
[画像: The team, three co-founders. Zicheng (Zhang Zicheng) builds the boards and firmware and runs production. Louis (Louis Huang) started Arduview as a project at Babson College. Liangyu (Ruan Liangyu) runs the community and answers your messages.]
Arduview began as my college project. I wanted a console where the inside is the best part, not something hidden behind plastic.
Thank you to the Arduboy community, whose games Arduview plays, and to everyone who put down a deposit before launch.
Louis Huang, co-founder
[画像: Get one from the first batch: hands playing a game on Arduview, its screen glowing above the clear board]
## Our Partners

The team behind Arduview was mentored by Funderce - months of personalized, step-by-step guidance through every phase of their crowdfunding launch. risks: Arduview exists as a working prototype. We have built three of them, selected our manufacturer, received production quotes, and arranged packaging and shipping. What is still ahead is tooling and the first production run, and that is where the risks sit. Tooling and production. The acrylic frame and buttons require moulds, and the production line needs tooling before anything can be made at volume. Adjustments during setup or the first run could move our schedule. We will review initial samples before committing to the full batch, and there is time in the plan for a second round if the first one is not right. Component availability and costs. Component prices, availability and supplier lead times can all change between now and production. We will reconfirm both before placing orders. If a part becomes unavailable we will qualify a replacement and tell you what changed, rather than substitute quietly. Testing and quality. Testing may turn up hardware, firmware or assembly problems. Clear parts are less forgiving than a black shell, because flow lines, sink marks and trapped dust all show. Every production sample gets checked for function and finish, and anything significant gets fixed before the batch runs. Shipping and delivery. Freight schedules, customs processing and local delivery conditions can all cause delays. Shipping dates and transit times are estimates, not promises. If any of this delays us, you will hear it from us first, with the reason and a revised date, in a project update. We post an update every month.

faq.q: Does it play Game Boy games or run emulators?
faq.a: No. It plays Arduboy games instead: 300+ games already on it, plus hundreds more free from the Arduboy community.
No. Arduview is independent. It is compatible with Arduboy's open-source platform, so the whole community library runs on it.

faq.q: Can I see the screen in daylight? In the dark?
faq.a: Yes to both. It is an OLED, so every pixel makes its own light.

faq.q: Is it distracting to see the room behind the game?
faq.a: No. The games are pure 8-bit: big, chunky pixels that are either fully lit or fully clear, nothing in between. It is extremely high contrast when lit, so the game stays crisp in front and the room stays behind it.

We have a working prototype, three of them so far, and the console in every photograph on this page is one of them. Production units have not been made yet. The funding pays for the moulds, the production-line tooling and the first production run.
No. Every console pledge includes the Arduview console, a USB-C cable and an instruction manual. The keyring and the display stand are add-ons you can put on any pledge.

faq.q: When will it ship, and what if it is late?
faq.a: Production runs in December 2026 and January 2027, and units are dispatched in February 2027. Average delivery after dispatch is about one working month. If anything moves, you will hear it from us first, with the reason and a revised date.
Tell us and we will make it right. You get a free replacement within 30 days of delivery.
Only if the campaign reaches its goal, and only when the campaign ends. Not before.

faq.q: Can I cancel or change my pledge?
faq.a: Yes, any time before the campaign closes.

faq.q: Will it run the Arduboy games I already have?
faq.a: Yes. It runs the existing Arduboy library as it is. Nothing needs re-flashing or converting.

faq.q: Where do you ship, and what does it cost?
faq.a: Worldwide, directly from China. Shipping is charged after the campaign ends, not with your pledge, by region: Asia HK$149 (about US$19), Europe HK$196 (US$25), North America HK$196 (US$25), South America HK$272 (US$35), Africa HK$272 (US$35), and everywhere else HK$306 (US$39).

faq.q: Can I order more than one?
faq.a: Yes. There are two-pack and four-pack tiers on this page, and the per-console price drops on both.

faq.q: I paid the $5 reservation. What happens now?
faq.a: A reservation is not a Kickstarter pledge. When the campaign opens you get a private link to the founder tier, and you back the project through Kickstarter from there. The reservation is refundable at any time before your console ships. Email louis@arduview.com.

faq.q: Is the screen readable, or does the background show through the game?
faq.a: The games are 8-bit: every pixel is either fully lit or fully clear, so contrast is high and the game reads in front of whatever is behind it. It is an OLED, so it works in daylight and in the dark.
